thread:
sam: Quick sync — ran a latency-economics sweep comparing streaming chat vs sync completions. Goal was p95 < 120ms and p99 < 250ms; we tested a handshake pacing tweak + batch sizes 1/2/4/8. Posting topline numbers and a couple traces.

maya: Nice. Topline p99s? any regressions vs baseline?

sam: Results snapshot (short):
```
policy              | stream p95 | stream p99 | sync p95 | sync p99 | tokens/sec
baseline-handshake  | 95ms       | 320ms      | 140ms    | 420ms    | 45k
paced-handshake     | 110ms      | 180ms      | 130ms    | 260ms    | 60k
batch-8-aggressive  | 160ms      | 420ms      | 80ms     | 190ms    | 120k
```
sam: TL;DR: paced-handshake improves stream p99 a lot with modest p95 hit; batch-8 kills stream tails but helps sync greatly.

ryan: Looks like tail is dominated by kernel warmup + KV lookups when stream is small-batched. Do we have kernel switch traces?

sam: Yep — perf-bot uploaded a trace to the internal collector and I pulled a flamegraph. Link: https://perf.internal/trace/4758001234 (viewable to eng-runtime)

perf-bot: Uploaded trace: trace_id=trace-4758001234; summary: main tail events = kernel-select(44%), kv-lookup-block(28%), gpu-wait(18%), syscall(10%).

ben: Kernel-select spikes when seqlen ~ <32 and batch inter-arrival jitter high. The runtime keeps switching to the small-seq kernel which has higher per-call overhead. That explains stream-tail sensitivity.

maya: Is the paced-handshake just delaying tokens to increase apparent batch? can we simulate its effect with a small-prefetch instead?

sam: paced-handshake adds a 6-12ms pacing window aligned to tenant handshake to allow microbatch coalescing without full 8-batch latency. It's effectively reducing kernel-switch churn. Prefetch reduces KV miss rate but doesn't help kernel-selection churn as much.

ryan: Quick experiment idea: add a kernel-hint when handshake header present (hint: prefer bulk-kernel if tokens in-flight > 1). That should avoid unnecessary switches. Any downside?

ben: Risk: mistaken hint could push sync paths into a slower kernel for short completions. Need canary + fallback if p99 starts rising.

maya: Can we get per-route p95/p99 split by tenant so we don't blow up economics on tail tenants? If paced-handshake helps 80% but regresses 20% we need per-tenant policy.

sam: I ran a tenant-split: paced-handshake improved 75% tenants' stream p99 by ~100-150ms, 18% neutral, 7% regressed by ~20-30ms. Sync customers mostly neutral or improved.

ryan: Action items: 1) implement kernel-hint pilot behind feature flag, 2) add per-tenant routing policy for paced-handshake, 3) add KV-prefetch metric to console to correlate misses with tail.

ben: Agreed. I'll prototype kernel-hint patch (runtime/kernel_selector.cc) and add a microsample trace annotation for when we force a kernel. Small testbed: c5-gpu_dev1.

sam: I'll schedule a short canary run tomorrow 09:30 PT and collect p95/p99 + tokens/sec. Will post follow-ups. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maya: Great. If we can hold stream p95 ~110ms and p99 <200ms with <10% throughput loss that's a win.

perf-bot: Canary created: canary-4758001234; start=2026-03-19T09:30:00-07:00; owners=[sam,ben]. Monitoring: /dash/latency-econ/4758001234

sam: leaving notes here after run — will paste final numbers and trace samples.
